set.tagline: Four agents, two warring ideologies, and a city block that may not survive the argument.
set.description: Bullfrog's 1996 action-strategy sequel sends a squad of cybernetically enhanced agents into the conflict between EuroCorp and the Church of the New Epoch. The GOG DOSBox release is sold for Windows and macOS and lists both solo and multiplayer play.

qualityBar.verdict: A grimy tactical action game where the plan is precise until four heavily armed agents turn a street into a crater.

set.longDescription:
Syndicate Wars sends a squad of four agents into a future where corporations and religious movements have turned whole cities into battlefields. Bullfrog's 1996 sequel trades the cleaner lines of the first Syndicate for a darker, more destructible world. Your agents arrive with weapons and cybernetic upgrades; the mission asks you to complete an objective while the streets provide a steady stream of things that can go wrong. Sometimes the right move is a careful approach. Sometimes it is realizing that the careful approach ended three explosions ago.

The two sides, EuroCorp and the Church of the New Epoch, give the campaign its shape. Each mission is a small tactical puzzle with an action-game pulse. You can direct agents as a group or pay attention to one, moving through buildings and city blocks that invite both planning and collateral damage. Research and equipment upgrades give your team new possibilities between assignments. The fiction is blunt and cynical, but the game is most memorable when its systems collide: a squad meant to slip through a street instead attracts every armed response in the district.

GOG's current commercial copy runs through DOSBox and is listed for Windows and macOS. It provides DRM-free offline downloads, so Galaxy is optional. The storefront marks both single-player and multiplayer, but a feature label is not proof that its DOSBox network configuration is ready for PlayBound's virtual LAN or automatic party handoff. We have not verified the exact connection steps and will not claim an integrated PlayBound join route yet. There is no confirmed PlayBound dedicated-server recipe or tested controller profile for this package. Mouse and keyboard remain the safe control recommendation for the PC edition.

The previous Draft showed a 2026 release year and copied the beginning of a store blurb into both its tagline and description. The actual release is from 1996. GOG's current Windows minimum lists Windows 10, a 1.8 GHz CPU, 2 GB RAM, DirectX 9.0c-class graphics and 2 GB storage; it does not publish equivalent numerical Mac requirements on the same page. Those are requirements for the modern DOSBox package, not an attempt to describe the original DOS computer. The archive size in the older catalog has not been independently checked against the current GOG download, so we are not presenting its placeholder as a verified installed footprint.

Syndicate Wars belongs here for players who want strategy with a dangerous amount of agency. Directing four augmented operatives is enough to make a plan; giving those operatives explosives is enough to make every plan temporary. The sharpest moments arrive when you decide whether to rescue a failing objective or let the city absorb the cost of your improvisation.
set.whyWePickedIt: Syndicate Wars makes squad tactics feel volatile. Its destructible future cities, competing factions and upgrade choices give each mission a story beyond the objective text. The GOG copy keeps it accessible on two desktop platforms, while its multiplayer remains a clear testing target before PlayBound party support is advertised.
set.thatOneThing: You order four agents to cross the street quietly, then learn the street is the only thing left standing quietly.

installSteps.text: Buy Syndicate Wars on GOG, download its Windows DRM-free offline installer, and install the DOSBox-powered package. GOG Galaxy is optional.
Buy Syndicate Wars on GOG and download the macOS package from your library. Follow the instructions supplied with that DOSBox-powered build.
After installing your owned copy, use PlayBound Locate to select the game installation. Launch a single-player mission before attempting multiplayer setup.

firstPlaySteps.text: Use the first mission to practice selecting individual agents, moving the full squad and checking equipment between assignments.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: GOG lists a multiplayer mode, but PlayBound has not yet verified this DOSBox package's network configuration or automatic party joining. Use the game's own multiplayer instructions and do not expect PlayBound to create a room automatically.
